# condition text

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:conditionText`](gmeow-conditionText.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/conditionText>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/norms`](../../slices/norms.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The natural-language statement of the condition — the canonical form, always present (SHACL). Formalizations approximate the prose, not the other way around.

## Structure

**Property shape:** datatype property; [`gmeow:Condition`](../classes/gmeow-Condition.md) -> [`xsd:string`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string); functional

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:conditionText`](gmeow-conditionText.md) from [`gmeow:Condition`](../classes/gmeow-Condition.md) to [`xsd:string`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to carry the canonical natural-language statement of a condition — always present, the form formalizations approximate.

### Avoid when

- Avoid omitting it (it is mandatory by SHACL) and avoid treating a machine formalization as the canonical form — that is a [`gmeow:ConditionExpression`](../classes/gmeow-ConditionExpression.md), a claim about this prose.

### How to use

- Assert [`gmeow:conditionText`](gmeow-conditionText.md) once per [`gmeow:Condition`](../classes/gmeow-Condition.md) with the prose statement; attach optional formalizations via [`gmeow:formalizedAs`](gmeow-formalizedAs.md) that each claim equivalence to it.

### Examples

- ex:c1 [`gmeow:conditionText`](gmeow-conditionText.md) "the data subject has requested erasure".
